title: Rep. Ciscomani honors final A-10 flight at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base
text:
Rep. Ciscomani honors final A-10 flight at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base
J. E. Carter
U.S. Representative Juan Ciscomani honored the final A-10 flight at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base in Tucson on July 29, marking the end of 50 years of A-10 operations at the base. The last flight was conducted by Lieutenant Colonel Ryan "Clutch" Rutter, commander of the 357th Fighter Squadron, and Lieutenant Colonel Rodney Dwyer, commander of the 355th Operations Group.
"Davis-Monthan Air Force Base and the Tucson community have a longstanding connection to the A-10," said Rep. Ciscomani. "Although A-10 operations at the base have now ended, the aircraft’s legacy will live on. For half a century, the A-10 aircraft played a pivotal role in our community. While it will no longer be used at Davis-Monthan AFB, the A-10 will forever remain and be remembered as a key component in our city’s history and military strength. Congratulations to Lieutenant Colonels Rutter and Dwyer, the 357th Fighter Squadron, and everyone at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base on today’s milestone and an impressive 50 years of A-10 operations!"
Among those attending was Sam Moreland, retired Air Force lieutenant colonel and former squadron commander for the 357th Fighter Squadron. "It’s an emotional event, seeing this mission end," said Moreland. "It’s near and dear to our hearts. We did it for the troops on the ground and I hope we never forget what this plane did." The event drew members from across Tucson's military community who recognized its significance.
TJ Hogan, a career A-10 pilot and graduate of the U.S. Air Force Academy in 1989, said: "The final A-10 flight at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base signifies the close of a crucial chapter in Tucson’s military history... As a former A-10 pilot, I understand firsthand the significance of operating this unique aircraft and how much of an honor it is to do so... I want to congratulate everyone at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base for half a century of A-10 operations." Ahead of this final flight event, Davis-Monthan celebrated its last graduating class of student pilots from its training squadron earlier this spring.
The completion of local operations reflects both historical significance for southern Arizona as well as changes within national defense priorities regarding use of specialized air support aircraft like the Thunderbolt II “Warthog.” Designed during Cold War tensions for close air support against Soviet tanks in Europe—and remaining unique among U.S. aircraft—the model continues serving national security needs elsewhere.
Ciscomani currently represents Arizona's 6th district after replacing Ann Kirkpatrick in Congress beginning in 2023; he was born in Hermosillo, Mexico in 1982 before earning his BA from University of Arizona in 2005, according to Rep. Ciscomani's office.
